records.issue_text: [BUG] The cleanup for the newly created "idp-alias-20" likewise calls testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove, referencing a non-existent alias. idp-alias-20 (later made login-available and org-linked by the test itself) is never cleaned up, leaking a broker with BROKER_PUBLIC=true into the realm for subsequent tests in the same suite.
records.rationale: In the new test `testCacheIDPForLogin`, cleanup is registered with `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` both in the loop creating `idp-alias-0`..`idp-alias-19` and again after creating `idp-alias-20`. The literal key passed to `.get(...)` is `"alias"`, not the actual alias string (e.g., `"idp-alias-20"`), so the newly created IDP(s) are not properly targeted for removal, plausibly leaking IDPs into subsequent tests.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The cache-hit path of getForLogin returns raw models from session.identityProviders().getById(id) while the cache-miss path maps results through createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, so the returned stream has different semantics depending on cache state. The first uncached call after invalidation returns organization-wrapped IDP models (which can override enabled/visibility per organization context), while all subsequent cached calls return unwrapped raw models — callers like OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean get different data for the identical request depending on whether the cache was warm; the method does not enforce the invariant that its result shape is independent of cache state.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The update-path invalidation optimization (registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate) relies on the assumption that the organizationId field and BROKER_PUBLIC config on the passed models capture every way an IDP's login eligibility can change, which the diff does not establish. Any write path that mutates login-relevant state without passing through this provider's update() (e.g. organization link changes driven through OrganizationProvider's own broker update, or direct config changes by other SPIs) leaves the .idp.login caches serving stale IDP lists until an unrelated invalidation; the skip-fast branch converts a previously-always-fresh lookup into a staleness window that the new test only exercises through the admin API.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The defensive re-check added to both branches only re-checks idp.isEnabled(), not the other criteria of the login predicate (hideOnLogin, org BROKER_PUBLIC), so a wrapped model that was made login-ineligible by any non-enabled criterion still passes the filter. A login page served from the cached getForLogin path can render an IDP that hideOnLogin or org-visibility rules exclude, and clicking it proceeds into a broker flow the admin explicitly hid — inconsistent with the predicate the cache is supposed to honor.
